parts.note: The target's statement, for any causality, any open W (the homotopy) and Ũ; no ladder property and no separation axiom. Proof: clamp Γ by max 0 (min 1 ·) to a continuous map on ℝ²; S = {t | Γ (clamp t) maps [0, 1] into Ũ} is open (tube lemma, IsCompact.eventually_forall_of_forall_eventually), contains 0, and closure S ∩ [0, 1] ⊆ S (a limit curve has its interior points in the closure of the diamond, the endpoints are fixed); [0, 1] is preconnected (IsPreconnected.subset_of_closure_inter_subset). Witness: timelikeLine_confinement.

The target's inclusion (…_subset_of_futureOneConnectedOn), and stronger: the diamond of W equals that of W ⊓ Ũ. W is CausallyArcConnectedOn W and FutureOneConnectedOn W (the On forms, weaker than the global ladder properties); the curve form needs only future one-connectedness. Witness: timelikeLine_diamond_identification (W = ℝ, Ũ = (−1, 2), x = 0, y = 1, γ = id; the diamond contains 1/2).

LocallyStronglyCausal as the target defines it (no clash: grep -w of Causal/ and scaffold/); StronglyCausal ⇒ LocallyStronglyCausal; on a locally compact R₁ (hence every locally compact Hausdorff) M, the closure hypothesis of (i), with compact closures, for all x, y in a neighbourhood V of every point, Ũ inside any given neighbourhood. The evidence's construction is followed, simplified: Ũ = W ∩ interior N, K' a compact neighbourhood of p in Ũ, V ⊆ K' causally convex in W; then J_Ũ(x, y) ⊆ J_W(x, y) ⊆ V ⊆ K', and in an R₁ space closure K' ⊆ Ũ (IsCompact.closure_subset_of_isOpen), so the first compact K of the evidence is not needed. With [RegularSpace M] alone the closures lie in Ũ (closed neighbourhoods). Witnesses: timelikeLine_locallyStronglyCausal, timelikeLine_exists_isCompact_closure; exists_confining_not_locallyStronglyCausal shows the property is sufficient, not necessary.

lemmas_for_the_keeper.role: candidates for the keeper, argued only. (1) The loop fan, Causal.loopFan (Causal/GHWithoutTarentin.lean:753): not strongly causal (loopFan_not_stronglyCausal, :877), absolutely minimal on every open set (loopFan_absolutelyMinimalOn, :804), T2 and second countable. Argued locally strongly causal: at a = (0, 0) take W = {height < 1/2}; an arc piece inside W stays on one leg of a tent (the peak is at height 1 + ε_n), along which both coordinates are monotone, so every box ∩ W is causally convex in W; at p ≠ a, a small box meets one tent only and is causally convex in M. Would refute locally_strongly_causal → strongly_causal in either reading of defi:causalite. It must go in a module other than CausalScaffold.DiamondConfinement, since Causal.GHWithoutTarentin imports Causal.Ladder.Rules (kb/0221). (2) The flat time cylinder (Causal.Model.FlatTimeCylinder, a model): ≪_M total, not strongly causal, small opens flat; argued locally strongly causal, would also give locally_strongly_causal ⇏ is_causal.

findings: No defect in the argument of (i)–(iii) as printed (Thm 3.1 Step 3, InexSchwarzschild2.tex:619–621; §1, :153–158; Thm 4.11, :1623): each was checked against the TeX and is proved in Lean in a form at least as strong.

Thm 3.1 Step 3 (:621) and §1 (:158): the closure hypothesis is on the diamond up to γ̃(0), whereas the homotopy ends at γ̃(−s₁) (§1: at γ̃(s), s < 0). The closedness of I then needs the curves of the homotopy in the larger diamond, i.e. γ̃(−s₁) ≪_Ũ γ̃(0) and transitivity of ≪_Ũ. That holds, since γ̃ is a timelike curve in Ũ on (−ε, 0] (Step 1.1 (1), :491), but it is not said. The Lean form is ChronalHomotopyOn.mapsTo_of_closure_subset_of_lt, through closure_Iplus_inter_Iminus_subset_of_lt.

§1 (:158), 'a homotopy as above cannot escape I⁺(γ̃(s₀), Ũ) ∩ I⁻(γ̃(0), Ũ)': this is literally false at the common initial point γ̃(s₀). That point is not in I⁺(γ̃(s₀), Ũ) when Ũ is chronological, which the near-Minkowskian chart is. The image of the homotopy lies in that diamond ∪ {γ̃(s₀)}. Harmless. ETT form: ChronalHomotopyOn.mem_Iplus_inter_Iminus_of_closure_subset (s ∈ (0, 1)).

Step 1.2 (:528–532) gives compactness of the closure in the chart (−ε, ε)^{d+1}. Step 3 (:621) uses 'the closure in M̃ is contained in Ũ', and Thm 4.11 (:1625) writes 'precompact in Õ, i.e., in particular its closure in M̃ is contained in Õ'. Passing from one to the other uses that M̃ is Hausdorff (a compact subset of Ũ is closed in M̃), which the standing convention gives (:228, 'All manifolds considered in this paper are Hausdorff'). Correct. ETT needs only R₁ (IsCompact.closure_subset_of_isOpen), or regularity if only closure ⊆ Ũ is wanted.
